requirement:
Each listed first-party Rust file in the combined file coverage
map MUST provide access to a file-notes view identifying its
workspace-relative path.
rationale: **Obligation.** `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` says each listed first-party Rust file in the combined file coverage map MUST provide access to a file-notes view that identifies its workspace-relative path. This splits into three checks: (a) the map links to a notes view, (b) that view exists as a book chapter, and (c) the view shows the file's workspace-relative path. **Tests mapped to the obligation** - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[gaps_union_process_locations_and_omit_per_test_reports]` builds a combined map with `code.rs`, `zero.rs` and `executable.rs`. - It computes the notes path with `notes::path`. - It asserts that the `code.rs` map row contains the matching `href`. - It asserts that a chapter at that path exists and contains `File: code.rs`. - It also asserts that every chapter after the index is named `File notes:…`. - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[gap_notes_use_current_source_without_collecting]` covers nested workspace-relative paths. - It checks `code.rs`, `src/a.rs` and `src/nested/a.rs`. - For each file it asserts that a notes chapter exists at the generated path and that its content contains `File: {file}`, so the view identifies the workspace-relative path. - Paths must be distinct from each other and from the index path. - Exactly one chapter exists per notes path. - `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs]` asserts `File: code.rs` in the rendered notes content and the per-entry `Source: code.rs:…` lines. - `unavailable_runs_are_readable_and_generated_paths_cannot_collide` also uses the notes path, but only to check collisions. **Possible gap, rejected.** Only the `code.rs` row's link is asserted in the combined map. I read `GapDirectory::render` and `populate_in` to check whether that leaves a hole. - The link, `chapter_href(index, notes::path(index, &file.file))`, is built unconditionally inside the per-file loop. It does not depend on measured versus not-measured status, so the `zero.rs` and `executable.rs` rows go through the same code as `code.rs`. - The notes pages come from `note_files`, which are the files with any obligations. That is a superset of the listed files, whose obligations are unaccepted. The second test confirms pages exist for multiple and nested files. - A plausible violation would be a notes link that breaks for some class of file. The reviewed tests cover the nested-path class for page existence and path content, and the `code.rs` link covers the link format. I found no distinct branch that could drop a link for one row type. I found no unacknowledged gap, and there are no `{fixme}` acknowledgments to account for.
